title: [fixed since r3] W4: motion-strip now has a real T1 drift net (check_manifest_prefix) wired where the strip path runs
evidence: manifest.odin:153 `check_manifest_prefix :: proc(demo_name: string, demo: ^Demo, catalog_hash: u64, logic_hz: i32,` ... motion_strip.odin:153 `append(&hashes, pp.state_hash(&state, state.events[before:], cat, context.temp_allocator))` ... motion_strip.odin:205 `check_manifest_prefix(demo_name, &demo, cat.hash, hz, hashes[:], &fails)`
detail: The r3 gap (no mechanical net on the strip path) is closed: per-stepped-tick hashes are collected during the strip run and prefix-checked against the blessed manifest, exit 2 on mismatch. Verified empirically both ways.
recommended_fix: N/A — fixed. Residual defect in the fix's hash-index convention reported separately as a fresh warning.

title: W4 fix misindexes: strip collects one hash per STEPPED tick but the manifest has one per WALL tick (paused ticks included) — false STATE DIVERGENCE on any paused demo
evidence: motion_strip.odin:141-153: `if !paused {` ... `append(&hashes, pp.state_hash(&state, state.events[before:], cat, context.temp_allocator))` (paused ticks append nothing). run.odin:400-406: `paused := paused_at(cfg.pauses[:], w, hz)` / `if paused {` ... `append(&hashes, pp.state_hash(&state, state.events[before:], cat, context.temp_allocator))` (paused wall ticks DO append the stable hash). manifest.odin compares positionally: `if hashes[i] != m.hashes[i] { append(fails, fmt.tprintf("T1: STATE DIVERGENCE at tick %d: ..."`. Empirically reproduced: `./bin/harness motion-strip pause 65000 71000 500 <dir>` → `motion-strip: T1 drift — T1: STATE DIVERGENCE at tick 1211: 568780a239c47780 != golden 09bbc05e1b830b64` — yet grep proves 568780a239c47780 IS the blessed hash at goldens/pause.t1 tick 1401 (the post-resume step); the timeline is not divergent. Also the frames are exported before the check runs (render_strip_frame at line 184 inside the loop; check at 205 after), so `refusing to emit a strip` is not literally true — all 12 PNGs were on disk after the failure.
detail: Any demo whose window extends past a resume (pause.dem, future paused demos) gets a false divergence verdict: the verb becomes unusable there and teaches operators the gate's STATE DIVERGENCE verdicts can be false alarms — undermining the exact trust the W4 net was built for.
recommended_fix: Match run_demo's per-wall-tick convention: append the paused-stability hash for paused wall ticks too (5-line fix), then the prefix aligns; optionally run the manifest check before exporting or delete the outdir on failure so 'refusing to emit' is true.

title: check_manifest_prefix duplicates check_manifest's header-verification block verbatim (~40 lines) and the copies already diverge
evidence: check_manifest (95): `if m.seed != demo.seed { append(fails, fmt.tprintf("T1: seed drift — manifest %d vs demo %d", m.seed, demo.seed))` ... `if m.ticks != i64(len(m.hashes)) { append(fails, fmt.tprintf("T1: manifest corrupt — ticks header %d but %d hash lines",`. check_manifest_prefix (153-176) repeats the version/seed/catalog_hash/logic_hz checks character-for-character but omits the `m.ticks != i64(len(m.hashes))` corruption check.
detail: Same-file copy-paste of the header checks; a future manifest header field must be remembered in both procs, and the copies have already drifted (corruption check present in one only).
recommended_fix: Extract a shared header-check helper (or a `prefix: bool` param on check_manifest) so the header logic lives once.
